analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־
Masculine plural absolute common noun with singular verbal agreement.

analysis.evidence: In וַיֹּאמֶר אֱלֹהִים אֶל נֹחַ (“God said to Noah”), אֶל introduces Noah as the person God addresses.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew preposition with no prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for נֹחַ linked to the root article nuach.
draft.definition: Noah, the son whom Lamech names in hope of relief from toil.
draft.evidence: Genesis 5:29 gives the name נֹחַ and explains it through the wordplay on יְנַחֲמֵנוּ, “he will comfort us.”

analysis.evidence: In וַיֹּאמֶר אֱלֹהִים אֶל נֹחַ, “God said to Noah,” אֶל introduces Noah as the person God addresses about the sign of the covenant.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew personal name with no prefix or suffix. The preposition אֶל is a separate word.

analysis.evidence: God tells Noah זֹאת אוֹת הַבְּרִית, “This is the sign of the covenant.” The following noun הַבְּרִית specifies what the sign marks.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew common noun of both genders, singular construct, with no prefix or suffix. The feminine singular זֹאת agrees with it here.

analysis.evidence: God addresses Noah and identifies the covenant as the one he established בֵּינִי וּבֵין כָּל בָּשָׂר, “between me and all flesh.”
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ precedes a feminine singular absolute noun. In אוֹת הַבְּרִית, “the sign of the covenant,” אוֹת is in construct.
analysis.sense: the covenant with Noah and all flesh

analysis.morphology: Indeclinable relative particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 67855:4, 67853:7, 67852:8.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew preposition with a first-person common singular pronominal suffix referring to God, the speaker.
analysis.sense: between (two parties): of covenant, sign, witness, strife

analysis.evidence: In בֵּינִי וּבֵין כָּל בָּשָׂר ‘between me and all flesh’, וּבֵין introduces all flesh as the second party to the covenant God established.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וּ ‘and’ joins the preposition בֵין ‘between’ to the preceding בֵּינִי ‘between me’.
analysis.sense: between (two parties): of covenant, sign, witness, strife
